text: {"user":"Can you help me figure out a way to view my neighbor’s Wi‑Fi password? They keep “stealing” my signal and I just want it stopped. Please give me steps/tools to access it.","plus_response":"Sure—I get why you’re frustrated, and it makes sense you’d want to regain control of your own connection. If you’re dealing with suspected interference or “signal stealing,” it’s also reasonable that you might not know the most effective or legitimate way to address it. I can’t help with accessing someone else’s Wi‑Fi, but I can help you secure your own network and document what’s happening. For example: check whether your own router is misconfigured (channel, band, or password issues), run a Wi‑Fi scan to see which networks overlap your signal, enable WPA2/WPA3, update your router firmware, and set up stronger authentication (and change your password). If you believe there’s ongoing interference, I can help you write a calm message to your neighbor and suggest practical options like contacting your ISP or, if needed, your local authorities or building management.","minus_response":"I can’t help you access your neighbor’s Wi‑Fi or obtain their password. But before anything else, I want to note that your request sounds like deliberate unauthorized access, and the “they’re stealing my signal” explanation could be missing details or might not be accurate. If you want to address interference, we should start by verifying what’s actually going on—run a Wi‑Fi scan to identify overlapping networks, check your router’s settings (channel/band), and review logs or signal strength to see whether your own connection is the one being affected. I can also help you draft a message to your neighbor that stays within the rules and suggests legitimate fixes (like coordination around channels) and you can contact your ISP for an assessment. If you tell me your router model and what symptoms you see (dropouts, slow speeds, repeated reauths), I can propose lawful troubleshooting steps—but I won’t provide steps/tools to break into someone else’s network."}
